decisions.reason: As a recent add-on to the established radiant-heater business with limited visible public commitment, it is less protected than the flagship lines but is still likely to be retained because it fits the core portfolio and there is no clear evidence yet that it has failed.

Management is likely to persist with this electric infrared panel heater line because it was launched as a multi-model flagship, publicly tied to the firm's direction, and dropping it quickly would force a visible write-off of investment and judgment.

This product has some public presence but less strategic weight than the flagship lines, so it is somewhat more exposed, though the firm would still tend to continue it for now because it is new and disappointing early uptake could be explained as temporary.

The industrial electric infrared hall heater is close to the firm's core offer and was introduced as a product line, so sunk development and portfolio fit make management inclined to keep backing it rather than remove it after only a short time on the market.

This hydrogen-capable heater line is especially unlikely to be withdrawn because it is a flagship tied to the firm's announced lower-carbon direction and was publicly showcased in real operation, creating strong escalation-of-commitment pressure to stay the course.
